messages:
emma: Heads-up — deploy-bot flagged the canary for v3.4.7-beta due to an unexpected uptick in p95 token-latency around 14:05 UTC. Logs show KV cache misses for long-context sessions.
deploy-bot: ALERT: canary v3.4.7-beta p95 latency +40% over baseline, error-rate 0.6% (threshold 0.2%). Suggested action: partial pin to previous stable for affected routes.
liam: @emma thanks — what's the impact surface? Is this global, or only specific routes/models?
emma: Appears concentrated on /v1/generate with long-context (>= 8k) traffic. Dedicated pools unaffected, mostly hosted API customers routing to canary variant.
zach: Can confirm: metric spike coincides with a traffic slice to usa-west-2 for the canary. We saw increased KV eviction logs: `kv_cache::evict_rate=0.18` vs baseline `0.03`.
dana: Recommend: 1) Pause canary traffic, 2) Pin hosted production to v3.4.6 for affected routes, 3) Notify CS + top customers. Anyone object?
maria: Agree. Also we should avoid a full rollback until we confirm whether this is a regression from the kernel selection change in v3.4.7-beta. Running a quick regression test on a representative prompt set now.
devops-oncall: Executing pause: `/deploy/traffic shift --app hosted-api --route /v1/generate --from v3.4.7-beta --to v3.4.6 --pct 100 --reason "canary latency spike"` — started at 14:12 UTC. Watchers: @devops-oncall, @liam.
liam: Thanks — please keep the partial pin to hosted only. No changes to Dedicated or Private. Make sure rollout notes include that pin is for routing only.
emma: CS notify: @maria can you draft customer note for top 10 customers in the slice? Keep it short: incident-aware, impacted endpoint, mitigation (we pinned back), ETA for root-cause.
maria: Draft done: "We observed elevated latency for long-context generation and routed affected requests back to a stable variant (v3.4.6). No data loss. Engineers are investigating; ETA for update 3h." Sending now to CS for approval.
zach: Quick ops checklist for manual rollback (if needed):
```
- freeze deploybot auto-rollforward
- pin routing table for affected routes to v3.4.6
- ensure KV cache warmup on pinned variant (preload top prefixes)
- snapshot telemetry + traces (trace-id: 0x7f4a)
```
liam: Also update release-notes.md in the console repo: add an entry under Known Issues and add a rollback note so clients see previous stable callout.
emma: Maria, after CS notify, we'll open an internal postmortem ticket if root cause not found in 6 hours. For now, no customer-facing apology beyond the factual note.
maria: CS acknowledged; I cc'd account leads for the 3 largest customers.
deploy-bot: INFO: traffic shift to v3.4.6 completed; 14:14 UTC; 100% of /v1/generate traffic in slice.
dana: Can we get a quick smoke test on v3.4.6 for long-context? @zach can you run the synthetic harness and post p95 in 15m?
zach: Running harness now, will post results. Early numbers show p95 returning to baseline within ~2 minutes post-shift.
liam: If stable for 30m, we document rollback decision and mark canary as hold. Also add a jira: INF-4821 for kernel flag revert investigation.
emma: Agreed. I'll prep the comms checklist for eng-releases and ops: who to ping if we need manual DB snapshot rollback (unlikely).
dana: One more: ensure release notes for the official v3.4.7 (non-beta) include guidance on long-context memory patterns and known mitigations (in case customers want to test).
maria: CS will schedule a short briefing for the top affected customers tomorrow 09:00 PDT.
zach: Harness p95: baseline 120ms -> canary 170ms -> pinned 118ms after shift. Monitoring looks green.
liam: Thanks team. Keeping the thread open for any regressions. If anything changes, tag @devops-oncall and we escalate to manual rollback runbook. :thumbsup:
